statement: For p,q arbitrary, let f_W(A,B)=<vec(AB^T)|W|vec(AB^T)> with A in C^(p x 2), B in C^(q x 2), and W Hermitian. Suppose the exact real-polynomial identity f_W(A,B)-gamma*||B||_F^2 = sum_j p_j(A,B)^2 + sum_(h=1)^4 g_h(A) b^* H_h b holds, where each p_j is real and bilinear separately in the real coordinates of A and of B, each H_h is a constant Hermitian 2q x 2q matrix, g_1,g_2 are the two column-norm-minus-one equations of A^*A=I_2, and g_3,g_4 are the real and imaginary offdiagonal equations. Then W-gamma*I is decomposable: P+Q^Gamma with P,Q Hermitian PSD. Consequently, if gamma>=0, such a certificate cannot certify any witness with negative expectation on a PPT state. In particular it cannot certify the actual rational KG candidate, whose negative expectation on the explicit PPT source is -27/100. This is an ansatz obstruction, not a claim that the candidate fails 2-block positivity or that the 4x4 target fails.
proof_phase_decomposition: Both f_W and the g_h(A) b^*H_h b terms are invariant under independent global phase rotations A -> e^(i theta) A and B -> e^(i phi) B. Average the identity over theta,phi in {0,pi/2,pi,3pi/2}. Write each real bilinear p as L_++(a,b)+L_+-(a,conj(b))+conj(L_++)+conj(L_+-), with L_++ and L_+- complex bilinear in the arguments shown. The finite average of p^2 is exactly 2|L_++|^2+2|L_+-|^2. Thus the averaged SOS has a PSD Gram P on a tensor b plus the Bob partial transpose Q^Gamma_(b) of a PSD Gram Q on a tensor conjugate(b). This finite averaging uses rational weights and does not change the left side or multipliers.
proof_slices: Regroup the biquadratic coefficient of f_W as M_W=W tensor [Omega_2] on (C^p tensor C^2) tensor (C^q tensor C^2). Comparing A-independent terms gives H_1+H_2=gamma I_(2q). Comparing biquadratic coefficients gives M_W=P+Q^Gamma_(b)+sum_h G_h tensor H_h, with G_h representing the corresponding A^*A entries. Slice auxiliary Alice |1> and auxiliary Bob |0>. The Omega term vanishes and only G_2 contributes, yielding 0=P_10+Q_10^Gamma_q+I_p tensor (H_2)_00, where P_10,Q_10 are PSD principal compressions. For every product |x> tensor |y>, the expectation of P_10+Q_10^Gamma_q is nonnegative; hence -(H_2)_00 is PSD. Slice both auxiliaries in |0>: W=P_00+Q_00^Gamma_q+I_p tensor (H_1)_00. Since (H_1)_00=gamma I_q-(H_2)_00, this is W-gamma I=[P_00+I_p tensor (-(H_2)_00)]+Q_00^Gamma_q, a decomposable representation. For any PPT rho, Tr(W rho)>=gamma Tr(rho).
scope: The statement covers arbitrary sums of real bilinear A/B squares, including mixed conjugation, but only the displayed equality multipliers b^*H_h b, and excludes ball terms or other multipliers/degrees. It does NOT establish a lower bound on all degree-four real SOS certificates, because general real quadratic squares and A-dependent or higher-degree multipliers are not included. The earlier complete rational Positivstellensatz hierarchy remains a distinct, unbounded route. WRITTEN; no independent review, formal verification, novelty clearance, or 4x4 conclusion.
